evidence.note: CONFIRMED. Claim: scan() reports "worktree is gone; nothing to salvage" for an item whose worktree path is gone WITHOUT counting its branch commits ahead of base. Refutation observation that would disprove: the Recovery for such an item already shows unmerged_commits>0/salvageable=True. Ran the new regression test against unfixed code: it FAILED with Recovery(item=T3, branch=ddflow/T3, salvageable=False, advice="worktree is gone; nothing to salvage. ddflow release T3 to clear the claim.") while ddflow/T3 held 1 commit main lacks. CONFIRMED.

Applied r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before reviews) and r-task-phase-needs-wave. Import layering: reused existing infra primitives (W.branch_exists, G.commits_ahead) and RepoFacts, no new infra file; change stays within recovery.py globs + the regression test.

Implemented in ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py: extracted _gone_tree + _branch_ahead; the gone-worktree path now counts the branch commits ahead of base (W.branch_exists -> G.commits_ahead) and reports them salvageable before falling back to nothing-to-salvage. Regression test tests/test_recover_merged_item.py::test_a_gone_worktree_whose_branch_holds_unmerged_commits_is_salvageable fails on unfixed, passes after. _measure kept at CC C (complexity ratchet).

chunk_findings.detail: `_branch_ahead` documents a return of -1 when the branch cannot be counted and says that value must never be folded into "empty", but `_gone_tree` only special-cases `ahead > 0`. Any other result, including -1 (empty `rec.branch`, or `G.commits_ahead` failing), falls through to `rec.advice = "worktree is gone; nothing to salvage"` and leaves `salvageable` unset. Given a missing worktree whose branch still exists but `commits_ahead` returns -1, recover tells the operator there is nothing to salvage — the same false empty verdict as B5b1c6272c1 — instead of leaving the row unmeasured the way the budget path sets `salvageable = None`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_gone_tree

data.probe: grok's -1/unknown finding: _gone_tree only special-cased ahead>0, folding -1 into nothing-to-salvage. Fixed: ahead<0 now sets salvageable=None + 'could not be measured' advice (guarded by test_a_gone_worktree_whose_branch_could_not_be_measured_is_not_called_empty).

evidence.note: roborev branch review (python -m ddflow.services.roborev_branch) ran: 0 unresolved findings after fixing the tri-state branch probe (absent vs unavailable) and the gone-tree path honoring the view budget.

chunk_findings.detail: `_branch_ahead` documents a three-way result (ahead, absent/merged, or unknown) but after `probe.unavailable` it treats every other non-zero `rev-parse` as “ref not there” and returns 0. Git uses exit 1 for a missing ref and 128 for fatal failures (not a repository, permission, `safe.directory`, corrupt/missing git dir). Given a gone worktree whose branch `ddflow/LS-worker-lane-override` still has unmerged commits, a 128 from `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/...` makes `_gone_tree` take the `ahead == 0` path and emit `worktree is gone; nothing to salvage`, which is the B5b1c6272c1 cleanup proposal again, not “could not be measured”.

data.probe: grok #1: probe exit-128 fatal errors folded into 'nothing to salvage'. chunk_findings.detail: A missing worktree now consumes the same `budget.take_tree()` slot as a live tree, which the previous early return did not. With `lease.scan_view_trees_max` of 1, scan item A (worktree path gone, branch fully merged or absent) then item B (worktree present, uncommitted salvageable work): A calls `take_tree()` and is classified empty, then B hits the budget path, sets `salvageable = None`, and is reported NOT MEASURED even though its tree exists and was never inspected. The view can therefore hide real uncommitted work while still declaring other rows empty.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_gone_tree

data.probe: grok rb #1: gone-tree spending a take_tree() slot could hide a present tree's real work behind a never-measured gone tree. Fixed: removed the budget param from _gone_tree; the branch probe is 2 cheap git calls, not the tree_work the budget caps, so it no longer spends a slot.
